correctness.rationale: Five distinct unit-circle zeros force every coefficient of a trigonometric degree-two Hermitian lift to vanish; after this reduction, three distinct second-circle zeros force every coefficient of the remaining degree-one trigonometric polynomial to vanish. The kernel is exactly real multiples of diag(R^2,-1-R^2,1), invertible when R>0. Rank-two pure-state differences cannot lie in it. A continuous odd determinant on a two-dimensional Hermitian nullplane gives the global seven-measurement impossibility. The singular-value approximation inequality gives the sharp rank-two projection gap, attained by deleting the smallest absolute diagonal eigencomponent. The standalone rational SymPy checker independently verifies a radius-two witness in exact arithmetic; infinite claims rely on the written proof.

value.rationale: This gives a globally minimal and angular-placement-robust two-radius sampling prescription for recovering arbitrary degree-two complex polynomial coefficients from plain intensity measurements. It exactly classifies the nontrivial one-dimensional Hermitian obstruction and computes the sharp rank-two separation from this kernel, which is the natural geometric obstruction governing pure-state identification. The conclusion is structural, parameter-uniform in node angles for injectivity, and distinct from simply repeating the known 4d-4 cardinality or presenting a finite numerical example. It does not assert an angle-independent output stability bound.
